Industrial ecologists (O*NET/SOC 19-2041.03, Industrial Ecologists) apply natural-ecosystem principles and processes to model efficient industrial systems, use physical and social science knowledge to maximize effective natural-resource use in producing and using goods and services, and examine societal issues and their relationships with technical systems and the environment. Official scope: Apply principles and processes of natural ecosystems to develop models for efficient industrial systems. Use knowledge from the physical and social sciences to maximize effective use of natural resources in the production and use of goods and services. Examine societal issues and their relationship with both technical systems and the environment. Core tasks include identifying environmental impacts of products, systems, or projects; developing strategies or methods to reduce industrial production impacts; analyzing changes to improve complex systems' environmental performance while avoiding unintended adverse effects; conducting sustainability assessments using material flow analysis (MFA) or substance flow analysis (SFA); identifying sustainable alternatives to industrial or waste-management practices; reviewing literature to maintain industrial-ecology knowledge; redesigning linear or open-loop systems as closed-loop systems, with waste becoming input for new processes in imitation of natural ecosystems; and writing environmental-impact and other technical reports and communicating findings to industry, government, and the public. Common titles include Ecologist, Environmental Consultant, and Research Scientist.
